title: Consecutive hybrids agree off the changed coordinate
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\Omega$ be a type, let $Z$ assign a real-valued function on $\Omega$ to each element of the disjoint union of two copies of the $n$-coordinate set, and let $i,j$ be coordinates with $j\ne i$. The hybrid families at stages $i$ and $i+1$ have the same function at coordinate $j$.
hypotheses_covered: $Z$ is a family of real-valued functions indexed by two disjoint copies of the $n$-coordinate set
replaced: Let $Z_{L,j},Z_{R,j}\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be two families indexed by $0\le j<n$, and put $H^{(r)}_j=Z_{R,j}$ if $j<r$ and $Z_{L,j}$ otherwise. If $i,j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and $j\ne i$, then $H^{(i)}_j=H^{(i+1)}_j$ as functions on $\Omega$.
